title: Natural comparison for constant set sheaves
statement: Let (C,JC) and (D,JD) be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let L ⊣ V be an adjunction between their sheaf categories of sets. If L preserves finite limits, there exists an isomorphism of functors constantSheaf JC (Type u) ⋙ L ≅ constantSheaf JD (Type u), with the constant functors of [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Thus the comparison is natural in every function of sets, not merely in ring homomorphisms. The module also defines its conjugation by constantCommuteCompose to the underlying set sheaves of constant commutative rings.

proof.text: The constant singleton sheaf is terminal: the constant presheaf singleton is terminal and set sheafification preserves finite limits. Since L preserves finite limits, L of this sheaf is again terminal. Take the unique isomorphism to the target constant singleton sheaf.

source.place: Tag 0H7J (Example example-constant-sheaf) and Tag 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi): constant sheaves and inverse image of algebraic structures

proof.text: Global sections of a set sheaf are represented by the constant singleton sheaf. The adjunction L ⊣ V and the preceding terminal comparison identify Γ_C(V F) with Γ_D(F), naturally in F. Apply uniqueness of left adjoints to the two adjunctions from sets to target sheaves: constant_C followed by L, and constant_D. This gives the required natural isomorphism. In Lean these are ΓNatIsoCoyoneda, compCoyonedaIso, constantSheafΓAdj, and leftAdjointUniq.

proof.text: For constant rings whisker with the forgetful functor and conjugate by constantCommuteCompose on the two sites. Naturality follows by composing the naturality squares of the three comparisons.
